experiment: optimal modality subset with the seventh task, all choices fold-internal
why: now known: motor hurts, EMOTION hurts, RELATIONAL helps. The candidate subsets are {+rel}, {+rel, -motor}, and the five. Choose among them inside the training fold.
verdict: THE BEST CONFIGURATION IS RELATIONAL IN, MOTOR OUT: +0.0174 in-fold (30/30, t = 25.5), the largest gain of the round, and a fold-internal rule reaches it on its own (225 of 300 folds). On 233 new subjects it is +0.0086 with CI [-0.009, +0.027] and P = 0.82 -- positive but not significant, and slightly smaller than the six-plus-relational arm's holdout (+0.0099, P = 0.94).
honest_read: the holdout cannot separate {+rel} from {+rel, -motor}: +0.0099 vs +0.0086, both inside noise. So the in-fold ranking (rel-no-motor ahead) is not confirmed out of sample, and the safe statement is the shared one: ADDING RELATIONAL HELPS, about +0.01 on new subjects; whether motor should also go is undetermined by this data.
what_this_means_for_the_config: choose {+rel, -motor} on in-fold evidence (it is the largest and the rule picks it), but report that the motor part is not confirmed out of sample -- exactly the same status motor had on its own.
